## Entries since `0.57.0`

## 2026-10-25 — v0.59.0

### Added

- **`webshot` emulates a named phone.** A `device` key, for the whole spec or one shot, takes a Playwright device name (`"iPhone 13"`, `"Pixel 7"`) and sets the viewport, scale factor, user agent, touch and mobile layout; before, a narrow `viewport` was a desktop browser in a small window. An explicit `viewport` or `device_scale_factor` at the same level still wins, and an unknown name exits 2 with the known ones. `manifest.json` records the device. Tests: new cases in `tests/webshot_test.sh` (3 fail against 0.58.1).
- **`webshot_audit` finds pages wider than a phone.** `webshot_audit <start_url>` (and `bin/webshot audit`) crawls same-host links and loads each page on `iPhone 13` and `Galaxy S8`, or the `--device` names given. A page fails when the document is wider than the viewport or an `h1`-`h3` is cut off inside its box; the JSON report names the overflowing elements, `--skip` drops path prefixes and `--shots DIR` saves a PNG per page and device; downloads (PDF, zip) are listed apart from load errors. Exit 1 on any finding. Tests: new cases in `tests/webshot_test.sh` with fixture pages under `tests/fixtures/webshot/audit/`.

### Fixed

- **`webshot_pdf` no longer hangs on a trailing option.** `webshot_pdf in.html out.pdf --format` (a value option with nothing after it) looped forever on a failing `shift 2` when called from a script without `set -e`; it now returns 2. Tests: a new case in `tests/webshot_test.sh` (times out against 0.58.1).

### Changed

- **CI runs once per push to a release branch.** `ci.yml` and `ci-macos.yml` ran on `push` to `release/*` and again on its `pull_request`, so every job ran twice (8 checks for 4 jobs on a release PR). `push` now covers only `main`, which still checks every merged commit. `ci.yml` also cancels a pull request's superseded run, as `ci-macos.yml` does; push runs are never cancelled. `ci-macos.yml` sets `CI=''` instead of `CI=` (actionlint SC1007).
- **Small hosts get a coding model for `code`.** `config/ollama_model_tiers.txt` names `granite4.1:3b` (2.1 GB, Apache-2.0) for the small tier of `code`, which fell back to the general-purpose `qwen3.5:4b`. Run CPU-only on ten tested functions and five code reviews with a planted bug, it passed 10 and named 4, at 10.0 tokens/s; `qwen3.5:4b` passed 9 and named 4 at 5.9. Standard, large and xlarge are unchanged. A small host that has only `qwen3.5:4b` gets `granite4.1:3b` from its next `select code`: pulled when `OLLAMA_PULL_MISSING` allows, otherwise exit 5 naming it; a `.env` that names a model keeps it. Tests: `tests/ollama_select_test.sh` (an 8 GiB host with no GPU gets `granite4.1:3b`; fails against 0.58.1).

## 2026-10-24 — v0.58.1

### Fixed

- **Packaging docs use the submodule path.** `docs/packaging.md`, `docs/usage.md` and `templates/packaging/README.md` ran `./vendor/script-helpers/scripts/...`, a path that existed only because ci-helpers' packaging workflows symlinked it; https://github.com/nikolareljin/ci-helpers/pull/309 removes that symlink. The commands now use `scripts/script-helpers`, where the README installs the submodule. https://github.com/nikolareljin/script-helpers/issues/219
- **Python test runs install `requirements-dev.txt`.** A project that keeps pytest in `requirements-dev.txt` got only `requirements.txt` installed: `local_test_python.sh` reported SKIP and `preflight.sh` passed without running the tests, and `ci_python.sh`, `ci_python.ps1` and `ci_django.sh` failed with "No module named pytest". Each now installs it after `requirements.txt` (or alone); an explicit `--requirements` still installs only the file it names. `preflight.sh` and the pre-push fallback in `run_repo_tests.sh` detect a Python project from it. Tests: `tests/local_test_python_requirements_test.sh` (stub venv; 4 of 5 cases fail against 0.58.0), new cases in `tests/ci_python_test.sh` and `tests/ci_django_test.sh`, and `ps/tests/ci_python_test.ps1` (Docker mode).
- **`build_rpm_artifacts.sh` works with a prebuild.** With `--prebuild`, it tarred the working tree into `packaging/rpm/build/SOURCES/`, inside that tree, so tar read its own growing output and failed with `file changed as we read it` (reproduced with a 30 MB tree), and the source carried the build directory. The tarball is now written outside the tree and moved in, and the build directory, an artifact directory inside the tree and every `.git` are left out. Tests: `tests/rpm_build_prebuild_test.sh` (the build and artifact directories are in the source against 0.58.0; skipped without GNU tar). Item 2 of https://github.com/nikolareljin/ci-helpers/issues/297
- **Node test runs set `CI=true`.** With no `CI`, `react-scripts test` and `vitest` (without `run`) started in watch mode and waited, so `preflight.sh` in a pre-push hook never returned. `local_test_node.sh`, the `npm test` fallback in `run_repo_tests.sh` (the pre-push path without script-helpers beside it), `ci_node.sh` (host, and `-e CI` into its container, which runs with `-t`) and `ci_node.ps1` now run the test step with `CI=true`. A `CI` the caller sets is kept, and an explicit `--watch` still watches. As in CI, Jest then writes no new snapshots: a test whose snapshot is missing fails. Tests: `tests/local_test_node_ci_test.sh` (stub npm, node and docker; 5 of 6 cases fail against 0.58.0) and `ps/tests/ci_node_test.ps1` (2 of 3 fail).
- **Scripts check out with LF on Windows.** With no `.gitattributes`, a clone under `core.autocrlf=true` (the Git for Windows default) checked every script out with CRLF, and bash failed with `set: pipefail: invalid option name` or `$'\r': command not found`. `.gitattributes` now sets `* text=auto eol=lf`, which also covers the hooks and `bin/` commands with no extension. Tests: `tests/line_endings_test.sh` clones with `autocrlf=true` (395 files with CRLF and a failing `commit-msg` hook against 0.58.0); CI runs it on Windows too. A checkout made before this keeps its CRLF files after a pull (389 of them); with no local changes, `git rm -r -q --cached . && git reset -q --hard` rewrites them with LF.

## 2026-10-24 — v0.58.0

### Changed

- **The Claude hook lets a private repository name private repositories.** A command that, as the hook reads it, stays inside one repository whose every remote is listed `private` skips the private-name check; credentials and PII are still checked. Containment is an allowlist: a leading `cd` picks the repository (only when `&&` or the end of the command follows it), every path and `gh -R` must stay in it (no write or `cd` after a `git` command that can rewrite the work tree, or after `cp` or `mv`), and only listed local commands, `git` subcommands and `gh pr|issue` subcommands count. Anything else gets the full check, including a private file as the body of an issue in a public repository. Inside a private repository, a command naming another private repository was refused. Tests: `tests/claude_hook_destinations_test.sh` (41 cases fail against the 0.57.0 hook).
